issues.description: nevra[0] uses the first character of the filename rather than the first letter of the package name, breaking Koji's directory layout for digit-prefixed names
issues.detail: Koji's canonical path uses the lowercased first letter of the package NAME (e.g., '3' for '389-ds-base', 'k' for 'kernel'). Using nevra[0] on the full filename string is fragile and may produce a 404 when filenames don't begin with the package name's expected first character. Parse the package name from NEVRA explicitly.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None, producing a malformed URL containing literal 'None'
issues.detail: When the arch regex doesn't match, the function returns None and the f-string builds '.../latest/None/Packages/...', silently emitting a broken URL into rpms.lock.yaml. The failure only surfaces at fetch time in CI. Raise an explicit exception or fail loudly when arch cannot be parsed.

issues.description: noarch packages are not handled and will produce invalid rewritten URLs
issues.detail: repoquery includes '--arch noarch' but the arches list omits 'noarch'. A noarch RPM URL won't match the regex, extract_arch_from_url returns None, and the constructed URL is invalid. Either add 'noarch' to the list, detect noarch from the NEVRA, or leave noarch URLs unrewritten.

issues.description: Race condition between bump-lockfile merge and coreos-koji-tagger is acknowledged but unmitigated
issues.detail: The PR description admits crafted coreos-pool URLs may not resolve until coreos-koji-tagger runs, causing transient 404s in Konflux. There is no retry, HEAD verification, or in-code documentation of this dependency. At minimum add a verification step or a source comment so CI failures are diagnosable.

issues.description: Substring check for coreos-pool URLs is brittle and inconsistent across functions
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only uses 'koji_url_base in url' while query_packages_location checks for 'coreos-pool'. Both are permissive substring matches that could misclassify URLs containing those tokens. Prefer url.startswith(koji_url_base) and use the same canonical check in both places.

issues.description: Arch list is hardcoded and duplicates information available elsewhere in cosalib
issues.detail: The list ['x86_64', 'aarch64', 'ppc64le', 's390x'] is hardcoded inside extract_arch_from_url, while cosalib already exposes arch enumeration via get_basearch and related helpers. New arches (e.g., riscv64) would silently break this path. Centralize the list or pass the known arch in from the caller.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR's URL-rewriting approach to work around the DNF5 baseurl bug is directionally sound but has several correctness issues that should be fixed before merge. The most consistent concerns are the fragile nevra[0] subdirectory derivation, silent None returns from extract_arch_from_url that produce literal 'None' in URLs, and missing noarch handling — all of which can yield invalid URLs in rpms.lock.yaml. The acknowledged race with coreos-koji-tagger is unmitigated and deserves at least a verification step or in-code documentation. Secondary cleanups include tightening the coreos-pool detection check and centralizing the hardcoded arch list.
